instruction.text: A pavement has triangle tiles. The sides of each tile measure 13 centimetres, 15 centimetres, and 17 centimetres. Use Pythagoras’ Theorem to determine whether the tiles have right angles.
Do the triangle tiles have a right angle?

A ladder is leaning against a wall. The length of the ladder is 5 metres, the height from the floor to the top of the ladder is 4 metres, and the length between the wall and the foot of the ladder is 3 metres. Use Pythagoras’ Theorem to determine whether the angle between the wall and the floor is a right angle.
Is the angle between the wall and the floor a right angle?

The rind is cut off a slice of watermelon to get a triangle. Its sides measure 15 centimetres, 12 centimetres, and 9 centimetres. Use Pythagoras’ Theorem to determine whether this slice of watermelon has a right angle.
Does the watermelon slice have a right angle?
A road sign with three sides has the lengths, 30 centimetres, 30 centimetres and 40 centimetres. Use Pythagoras’ Theorem to determine whether this sign has a right angle?
Does the sign have a right angle?
